name: Strix
summary: Autonomous multi-agent AI pentester that runs targets dynamically in a sandbox, validates findings with working proofs-of-concept, and can scan in CI/CD. Open-source core with separate paid cloud and enterprise editions.
notes: Commercial editions exist; the free open-source edition is the Apache-2.0 repo. About 72k stars on 2026-11-07.

name: Shannon
summary: White-box AI pentester for web apps and APIs: reads source code, maps attack paths, then exploits the running app and reports only exploit-confirmed findings (PDF, Markdown, SARIF).
notes: AGPL-3.0 (strong copyleft; network use triggers source-sharing). Keygraph sells Pro/Enterprise editions and offers commercial licensing. Not accepting external code contributions. About 49k stars.

name: PentAGI
summary: Self-hosted fully autonomous multi-agent penetration-testing system (Go backend, web UI) that plans and runs security tools inside Docker.
notes: Repo also ships EULA.md and NOTICE files alongside the MIT LICENSE; read them before commercial reuse. About 32k stars.

name: Autonomous AI SOC Analyst
summary: Tier-1 SOC agent that ingests Sysmon, CloudTrail and Zeek telemetry, enriches indicators, builds an attack graph and issues a true/false-positive verdict with containment suggestions. Runs with a local LLM via Ollama.

name: AI-Powered SOC Alert Triage Agent
summary: Capstone-style triage agent built on Hermes Agent: selectively enriches IOCs with free threat-intel APIs, maps behaviour to MITRE ATT&CK and outputs a ranked triage report.

name: Vigil
summary: Open-source agentic SOC with a dozen specialist agents (triage, investigation, hunting, forensics, threat intel, malware and network analysis), Markdown playbooks and MCP-based integrations. Keeps a human approving response actions.
notes: License taken from the project's own wiki; confirm on repo.

name: AI Agent SOC Triage
summary: Python triage agent that classifies alerts against MITRE ATT&CK, scores severity, extracts IOCs and can run response playbooks; works with Splunk, Sentinel and Elastic.

name: AI-SOC (research implementation)
summary: Dockerised reference implementation of an LLM-augmented SOC covering alert triage, RAG-based threat intelligence over MITRE ATT&CK and log summarisation, grounded in a published survey.

name: Agentic-DFIR
summary: Autonomous DFIR agent for the SANS SIFT Workstation that enforces evidence-integrity rules in its architecture (typed forensic operations) rather than relying on prompts, and produces a traceable report.
notes: A sibling project page appears under the name Agentic-DART, likely an earlier name. License taken from project wiki.

name: Anthropic-Cybersecurity-Skills (community)
summary: Large library of structured cybersecurity skills (800+ across ~30 domains) for AI agents, following the agentskills.io standard and mapped to frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK and NIST CSF.
notes: Community project: the name uses 'Anthropic' but a third-party landscape list describes it as unofficial. Listing it does not imply Anthropic endorsement.

name: CAI (Cybersecurity AI)
summary: Open framework for building cybersecurity agents with hierarchical multi-agent patterns, aimed at bug bounty and autonomous pentesting; basis of several research papers.
notes: Archived status comes from a third-party landscape list; confirm on repo.

name: AgentDFIR
summary: Forensics for AI agents themselves: collects and reconstructs activity from Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Gemini CLI and Copilot, and flags orphan agents, cross-agent messaging and destructive commands. Go CLI.
notes: Different angle from other DFIR entries: it investigates AI-agent incidents.
